children: slipped 0.34% premarket as Reuters reported that the largest US automaker is sitting out a hybrid boom, with a single hybrid model in its lineup. In late 2024 Mary Barra said the automaker would have plug-in hybrids in North America by 2027. Supplier sources and forecasting firms expect nothing on sale in the US until near the end of the decade. Asked this month, Barra told Fortune GM would have hybrids in important segments but gave no time frame. A GM spokesman declined to comment on the forecasts.

GM currently sells one hybrid, the Corvette. Hybrids took 19% of US retail vehicle sales in August, up from around 16% before the Iran war pushed gasoline prices up roughly 40%, and reached 20% in May. JD Power found hybrids left dealer lots more than twice as fast as non-hybrid gas cars in the second quarter.

The share position has moved with it. GM's US market share fell to 16.8% in the first half from 17.6% a year earlier, while Toyota and Honda gained. Toyota reported electrified vehicles passing half its sales for the first time. Nissan is pulling forward a hybrid Rogue by several months, citing consumer demand. GM offers gas-only versions of the compact SUVs where most of that competition sits, including the Chevrolet Trax and Buick Envista.

title: GM Is Missing Out on the Hybrid Boom
